subtopics.title: Economic, Energy and Payments Cooperation
subtopics.summary: The 23rd annual summit adopted Programme 2030 to diversify India-Russia ties beyond defence and energy. The programme sets a trade target of $100 billion by 2030, against $68.7 billion recorded in 2024-25. Cooperation also covers national-currency settlements, payment-system interoperability and continued support for nuclear energy projects.
facts: Programme 2030 adopted to diversify ties beyond defence and energy.
Coordinated by the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technical and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC).
IRIGC-TEC is chaired by India's External Affairs Minister and Russia's Deputy Prime Minister.
Trade target: $100 billion by 2030.
Trade stood at $68.7 billion in 2024-25.
Settlements in national currencies to be boosted.
Work on interoperability of payment systems and CBDCs to bypass Western financial systems (SWIFT).
Negotiations on an FTA with the Eurasian Economic Union to be fast-tracked.
Continued support for Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, Small Modular Reactors and future civil nuclear projects.

subtopics.title: Defence and Strategic Cooperation
subtopics.summary: India and Russia focus on joint R&D, co-production under Make in India, military technology transfer and regular exercises. The RELOS agreement provides mutual logistics support for troops, warships and aircraft during operations away from home bases. The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue aligns foreign and defence ministers on strategic priorities.
facts: RELOS: Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement, enabling mutual logistics support for troops, warships and aircraft.
RELOS scope: access to each other's military facilities, ports and airspace.
RELOS includes simplified refuelling and maintenance support for deployments.
Russia was India's main supplier of defence equipment (36%).
India-Russia 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue aligns Foreign and Defence Ministers.
Joint exercise: INDRA.
BrahMos: cruise missile jointly developed by DRDO and NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM).
S-400 Triumf: long-range surface-to-air missile system procured by India.
Su-30MKI multi-role fighters produced in India by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

subtopics.title: Connectivity and Logistics Corridors
subtopics.summary: The proposed Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor aims to cut transport time to Russia by 40 per cent and saves 3,028 nautical miles over the existing route. The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) is a multi-modal route set up in 2000 by Iran, Russia and India. India-Russia Far East and Arctic cooperation is guided by a 2024-2029 programme.
facts: Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor is a proposed sea route passing through the Sea of Japan, South China Sea and Malacca Strait.
Aim: reduce transportation time to Russia by 40%.
Time saving: up to 16 days.
Distance saving: 3,028 nautical miles.
INSTC: multi-modal transportation route established in 2000 in St Petersburg by Iran, Russia and India.
INSTC aim: promote transportation cooperation among member states.
India-Russia Far East Cooperation Programme covers 2024-2029.
Key Far East and Arctic areas: agriculture and mining, manpower and pharmaceuticals, diamonds and shipping.
India is an Observer in the Arctic Council.

subtopics.title: Diplomacy, Counter-Terrorism and Honours
subtopics.summary: India and Russia signed a Treaty of Peace and Friendship in 1971 and a new Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation in 1993 after the Soviet Union dissolved. Both sides denounced the 2025 Pahalgam and 2024 Crocus City Hall attacks and called for strict action against UN-listed terrorist organisations. PM Modi was conferred Russia's Highest National Award, the Order of St Andrew the Apostle.
facts: Treaty of Peace and Friendship signed in 1971.
New Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation signed in 1993, after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
PM Modi was conferred Russia's Highest National Award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle.
Order of St Andrew established by Tsar Peter the Great in 1698, reinstated in 1998 and abolished in 1918.
Ganga-Volga Dialogue: platform to enhance Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership; organised by the Ministry of External Affairs with Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation.
Counter-terrorism: Pahalgam attack (2025) and Crocus City Hall attack (2024) denounced.
Both parties called for a Zero-Tolerance Policy and finalisation of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism.
Russia formally joined the International Big Cat Alliance.
Russia reiterated support for India's permanent membership of a reformed and expanded UN Security Council.

quizzes.passage:
India and Russia used their 23rd Annual Summit in New Delhi to widen cooperation well beyond their traditional areas. The summit came after the two countries upgraded their ties to a special and privileged strategic partnership, and it marked 25 years of that relationship. The leaders adopted a comprehensive programme meant to diversify bilateral ties beyond defence and energy. Its work is coordinated by a commission that handles trade, economic, scientific, technical and cultural cooperation between the two governments, and that body serves as the apex forum for economic dialogue between them.

Trade and finance formed a central part of the discussions. Both sides agreed to boost settlements in national currencies, and they decided to work on interoperability of their payment systems and digital currencies. Officials described this as a way to reduce reliance on Western financial channels. The leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to energy security, with continued support for nuclear power projects in India, including small modular reactors and future civil nuclear work.

The summit also addressed terrorism. Both countries called for strict action against all UN-listed terrorist organisations and endorsed a zero-tolerance approach grounded in international law. Connectivity and mobility were additional priorities, as the two governments pursued new routes for cargo and skilled professionals.

quizzes.passage:
Defence cooperation remains one of the strongest pillars of India's partnership with Russia. The two countries have agreed on a reciprocal logistics arrangement that allows their armed forces to draw mutual support while operating away from home bases. Under this arrangement, each side can access the other's military facilities, ports and airspace, and it provides simplified refuelling and maintenance for deployments.

A high-level dialogue that brings together the foreign and defence ministers of both countries helps align their strategic priorities. Russia has long been among India's largest suppliers of defence equipment, and the two sides continue to pursue joint research, co-production under Make in India and transfer of military technology. Regular joint exercises between the armed forces add to this cooperation, and recent frigates have been commissioned into the Indian Navy.

Several major platforms reflect this partnership. A cruise missile is being developed jointly by an Indian research organisation and a Russian design bureau, while Indian production lines build multi-role fighter aircraft and main battle tanks based on Russian designs. India has also procured a long-range surface-to-air missile system from Russia, and a former Russian aircraft carrier has been refurbished for the Indian Navy.
